study_identification_part.si4_title: Predicting Mental and Neurological Illnesses Based on Cerebellar Normative Features

study_characteristics_part.sc1_study_objective: Evaluate whether deviations from cerebellar normative models across multiple atlases (lobular and voxelwise) predict ASD, BD, SZ, MCI, and AD, and identify contributing cerebellar regions.

clinical_application_and_analysis_part.caa7_association_analysis: Logistic regression with stratified 5-fold cross-validation; AUROC as primary metric; additional metrics (precision, recall, sensitivity, specificity, balanced accuracy, AUPRC); permutation testing with 1,000 label shuffles for significance; comparison to Random Forest and feature importance via LR coefficients.
clinical_application_and_analysis_part.caa8_key_findings_brief: Cerebellar normative features moderately predict ASD and SZ (AUROC ~0.56–0.65) but not MCI, AD, or BD.
clinical_application_and_analysis_part.caa9_key_findings_detailed: Across anatomical, task-based, hierarchical, and resting-state atlases, AUROC for ASD and SZ reached ~0.56–0.65 and exceeded chance by permutation testing, while MCI/AD/BD did not. For SZ, median and variance from voxelwise deviations summarized within ROIs were most predictive; for ASD, lobular volumes and voxelwise variance were most predictive. LR and RF yielded similar performance and feature importance patterns.
clinical_application_and_analysis_part.caa11_application_notes: Controls matched to clinical cohorts by sex and site with age (MatchIt); baseline scans only; multiple cerebellar atlases used for interpretability; cerebellar normative models available via PCNportal; code references include PCNtoolkit, FreeSurfer, FSL, ACAPULCO, and SUIT.

caa10_key_limitations.answer: Predictive performance was only moderate for ASD/SZ and at chance for MCI/AD/BD; algorithmic details of the pre-trained normative model are not provided here; no explicit normative-model validation metrics (e.g., EV, MSLL) reported in this paper; analyses focus on cerebellar features and may miss extracerebellar information.

general_note_part.gn1_general_notes: The clinical group sizes reported in the Abstract (ASD 317; BD 238; SZ 195; MCI 122; AD 116) differ from Supplementary Table 2 totals (ASD 900; BD 277; SZ 312; MCI 122; AD 146), which sum to the stated clinical set size (n=1,757). We record the full clinical set values and note this discrepancy. The pre-trained cerebellar normative model spans ages 3–85 and accounts for age/sex/site; detailed modeling (e.g., HBR vs GPR) is deferred to Kim et al., 2024 (Nat Mental Health).
